![](thumbnail.png)

## Overview

This figure asks whether Brazil's main private-sector student aid programs (ProUni scholarships and FIES loans) kept pace with the explosive growth of distance-learning (EaD) enrollment. Rather than looking at the raw number of students covered by aid, it looks at what fraction of private enrollment, within each mode of delivery, is covered — a more policy-relevant way of asking whether aid reached where the system actually grew.

## Methodology

Drawn from the same SEDAP+ extraction as the enrollment-by-sector-and-route figure. The quantity plotted is a ratio within each mode of delivery (distance vs. in-person): enrollment holding a ProUni scholarship or a FIES loan, over all private enrollment in that mode. Public-sector enrollment is excluded, since a seat that carries no price cannot be described as covered or uncovered by aid. In absolute terms, ProUni coverage in distance learning looks stable — but the ratio shown here reveals that the same absolute count covered a shrinking fraction of a modality that more than doubled in size, which is the more policy-relevant reading of whether the aid instruments reached where the system actually grew.

## Pipeline

Run these scripts in this order, from the project root (each one writes to `data-raw/`, which the next one reads):

1. [`shared-pipeline/sedap/010_SEDAP_Cliente.R`](../../shared-pipeline/sedap/010_SEDAP_Cliente.R) — SEDAP+ API client, sourced by the script below — requires the `SEDAP_TOKEN` environment variable
2. [`shared-pipeline/sedap/020_Extrair_Nicho_2020_2024.R`](../../shared-pipeline/sedap/020_Extrair_Nicho_2020_2024.R) — extracts enrollment by sector × access route × shift/modality from the SUP_ALUNO tables 2010–2024 via SEDAP+ and writes `data-raw/INEP/derived/nicho_agregado_sedap_2010_2024.csv`
3. [`plot.R`](plot.R) — reads `data-raw/INEP/derived/nicho_agregado_sedap_2010_2024.csv`; writes the figure to `output/figures/descolamento-ead-politicas/` — compare it with this post's `thumbnail.png`

The SEDAP+ steps only run with an approved INEP credential exported as `SEDAP_TOKEN` (see Reproducibility below); the extracted CSV is not redistributed here.

## Reproducibility

**Tier: B**

This pipeline depends on restricted INEP data accessible via SEDAP+ credentials (`SEDAP_TOKEN` environment variable). Without an approved credential, the scripts in `shared-pipeline/sedap/` will not run — the logic remains available for audit, but full reproduction requires requesting access.
